rationale: Sourced correction and frontier cleanup while the N<=3 fast-path Candidate stays active. Reading handlePreAcceptReply again showed that the committed vector is not the leader's own proposal vector: the merged (seq,deps) produced by mergeAttributes are written back into the leader bookkeeping (lb.deps/lb.seq = merged while lb.status <= PREACCEPTED_EQ) before the branch is chosen, and both the fast-commit branch and the accept branch then install that merged vector. The N<=3 Thrifty exemption therefore does not change which vector is published; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equals that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either certifies agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. The Candidate's premise is corrected accordingly, and the exposure is now stated precisely: the leader's own record keeps the proposal ballot as vbal while a pre-accepting peer records the same pre-accept ballot, so a recovery selecting by vbal cannot prefer the committed vector over a strictly smaller one held by a peer. In the same product, the two recovery open details are resolved as unreachable dead code in the map (sub-case 4 never runs, taking with it bcastTryPreAccept, handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply, the possibleQuorum bookkeeping and the deferMap check), and B4 now records the merge-installation guard.

feedback.answered: Two sourced results. First, a correction of the active Candidate's premise: the fast path publishes the merged vector, not the leader's own proposal vector, because handlePreAcceptReply installs lb.deps and lb.seq from mergeAttributes before choosing the branch (lb.deps/lb.seq = merged while lb.status <= PREACCEPTED_EQ) and both the fast-commit branch and the accept branch then copy those merged values into the instance (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). allEqual is therefore not the check that decides which value is committed but the check that certifies every counted reply already holds that merged value; with the N<=3 Thrifty exemption the leader may publish a merged vector that no other replica holds at that ballot (the merged vector strictly dominates each reply's vector whenever a reply contributes a dependency the leader's own vector lacks). Second, the TryPreAccept open details are resolved as unreachable rather than as defects: sub-cases 3 and 4 of handlePrepareReply carry identical guards so sub-case 3 always wins, bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, and the whole path (handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply, possibleQuorum, deferMap) is dead; weaker pre-accept support falls to sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

whether such a re-commit changes the execution order of conflicting instances (the difference is a dependency component, so it decides whether the instance waits for a conflicting command), and therefore whether the exemption can produce divergent committed vectors for one instance
